Subject: Legacy API Bridge retirement — ops questions and exemption inventory

Team —

Quick one to surface a few operational unknowns ahead of the Legacy API Bridge retirement (planned Q3 cutover window). We have a growing list of customer requests for extended grace periods and a handful of technical caveats that could qualify as exemptions. Before I draft external comms I need clarity on the following from Product/Engineering/Sales: 

1) Exemption policy: what are the formal criteria for granting an opt-out (e.g., regulated data, on-prem appliance, active procurement/contract constraint)? Need a checklist we can run against accounts.

2) Timeline flexibility: is there an approved mechanism for pushing a single-customer bridge window beyond the general sunset date? If so, what SLAs or mitigation must they accept (no SLA, higher cost, enforced read-only)?

3) Technical escape hatches: what shim behavior will we support during the transition? Are there kernel/quantization compatibility concerns that would make a 'bridge' impossible for some models?

4) Comms lane: proposed cadence for proactive customers (dedicated vs hosted). Who owns the first customer outreach? Sales or CS?

I'm copying Laura for visibility on exemptions that may need executive approval. I've attached an initial tracker template (exemption_tracker.xlsx) — please update with any known accounts and flags.

Ask: reply with bullets against 1–4 by EOD tomorrow so I can produce an internal comms draft.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Legacy API Bridge retirement — ops questions and exemption inventory

Thanks Neha — good list. High level from Product: 

1) Exemption policy: Product will approve exemptions only for: (a) legally constrained customers where data residency/KMS prevents migration, (b) customers with active multi-quarter procurement that blocks planned engineering work, and (c) customers on dedicated capacity with validated incompatibility. We'll require a signed "Extended Bridge Addendum" with defined end-date and cost delta. I'll draft the checklist; attaching a short template to the drive link (will paste into the tracker).

2) Timeline flexibility: We can grant 3-month extension windows by default; anything beyond 6 months requires exec sign-off and a rolling mitigation plan. Extensions will come with a reduced SLA and a surcharge to cover maintenance.

3) Technical escape hatches: We intend to support a shallow shim for protocol compatibility (v1->v2 adaptor) for hosted customers where possible. For dedicated/private deployments, engineering must run a compatibility test — if the customer's model relies on legacy kernels/quantization paths that we cannot emulate, then the bridge is not feasible.

4) Comms lane: Sales should own outreach for top-tier accounts (book-of-record), CS owns ongoing migration sequencing. Product will provide standardized language. For public notices, Marketing will run the broad comms once we lock dates.

I'll update the tracker with proposed policy rows and sample wording by end of day.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, API

Technical notes to help scope exemptions: 

- Shim behavior: the adaptor will translate v1->v2 call framing and do best-effort mapping of function-calls. It is not a full runtime translation layer — we cannot emulate different KV cache semantics. Expect edge cases with streaming APIs and function-calling payloads.

- Kernel/quantization compatibility: if a customer's model is quantized with a custom kernel we do not ship, fallback to an unoptimized path will likely break latency SLOs. We should use a triage test: provide a small compatibility harness (2–3 test prompts) to the customer's infra team; if the harness fails, mark "incompatible".

- Suggested mitigation: for dedicated/private customers, offer a small temporary compatibility VM that runs our legacy kernel package for a fee; for hosted customers, offer a diagnostic run with a temporary flag that falls back to legacy runtime (no SLA).

Code snippet for triage harness (very short):

--BEGIN SNIPPET--
curl -X POST https://diagnostics.redwood/api/compat-check \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -d '{"model_name":"customer/model-x","prompts":["Test 1","Test 2"]}'
--END SNIPPET--

If Product wants I can own creating the harness and the small infra hook.

—Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks all — this is the sort of cross-functional clarity I wanted. Two operational notes from leadership: 

1) Strategic accounts (BrightBank class) — I'm willing to approve exceptions beyond the 6-month cap on a case-by-case basis if Sales commits to a migration playbook and an executive check-in cadence (monthly). Please flag any account that needs >6 months with clear commercial tradeoffs.

2) Executive summary — Neha, please produce a one-page Exec Summary summarizing exemptions requested, risk level, expected revenue at risk, and recommended decision (approve/deny/modified). We should have that by next Tues EOD so I can sign off on any >6-month asks.

If anyone surfaces a compliance/legal blocker, loop in Security immediately.
